creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`replace()` declares `-> str`, but its `regex=true` path raises RAD20024 on an uncompilable pattern. `matches()` is honest about the same situation with `bool|error`. The checker therefore can't warn anyone that `replace(s, pat, r, regex=true)` is fallible.

Deliberately left alone when the literal-default flip landed: widening it to `str|error` pushes an error union into every existing `replace()` call site, and expressions like `replace(a, b, c) + "!"` would stop type-checking. The unhandled-fallible hint is strict-only (`strictOnlyCodes` in `rts/check/check.go`), so the noise is bounded, but the type change itself is not.

The flip did shrink the exposure - the default path can no longer fail at all - so the honest signature only matters for `regex=true` calls. Worth deciding whether that's enough to justify the churn, or whether the answer is a different shape entirely.
title: replace() declares -> str but can error
